description.short: Rare Dan Cong with the spicy-floral fragrance of wild ginger lily blossoms
description.overview: One of the less common Fenghuang aroma cultivars, combining heady florals with a gentle spicy, ginger-like vibrancy in its aromatic profile.
description.aroma: Spicy-floral, with distinct notes of ginger blossom
description.taste: Spicy-floral and full-bodied, with a faint peppery warmth against a sweet backdrop
description.processing: Classic Dan Cong craft: withering → shaking → kill-green → rolling → baking/roasting

history.origin: Named after its aromatic resemblance to the fragrant ginger lily flower (Jiang Hua), used purely as an aromatic descriptor rather than an additive or flavoring ingredient.
history.development: One of the rarer xiangxing lineages found only on a limited number of mature trees across Phoenix Mountain.
history.modern: Due to limited production, it is typically released in micro-batches and sought after by Dan Cong connoisseurs aiming to taste the full spectrum of Fenghuang aromatic types.
interestingFacts: The full catalog of recognized Fenghuang Dan Cong aroma profiles continues to be refined by local tea associations; Jiang Hua Xiang remains one of the least documented outside of China.
